text:
karthik: Quick flag — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak I'm seeing p99 regressions on long-seq routes. Spike ~40% on a small subset of requests that set max_tokens >= 1024. attaching profiler summary.

dylan: saw similar in my dashboards. canary was bumped to microbatch_ms=32. stack traces show extra kernel-fallback copies happening mid-generation which lines up with the p99 tail.

emily: can you paste the canary config you rolled? small snippet helps reproduce.

karthik: sure — this is what went to canary:
```json
{"scheduler": {"microbatch_ms": 32, "kernel_policy": "latency-weighted"}, "kernel_picker": {"enable_dynamic_padding": true}}
```

maria: reproduced locally by replaying ~2k long-seq requests. p50 stable, p99 jumps. KV cache hit-rate drops for requests where we hit the fallback kernel path (cache keys differ after padding/truncation changes).

sophia: short-term mitigation idea: enforce a dynamic per-route max_tokens cap at the frontend and apply an explicit truncation strategy before scheduling. this prevents stragglers holding microbatches and forcing kernel flips.

sophia: example config we'd push as a canary:
```yaml
routes:
  /v1/chat/completions:
    max_tokens_override: 512
    truncation_strategy: trim_front
    reject_on_truncate: false
```

dylan: another quick win: pin kernel selection for sequences > 512 to the "seq-optimized" kernel. avoids the runtime doing an expensive recompile/fallback when the microbatcher mixes long+short sequences.

karthik: ops — can we run a canary with the route cap + kernel pin for the two highest-p99 routes? @deploy-bot schedule pls.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for canary/eng-runtime. commit: abc123, rolling 10% -> 100% if stable. will post status when done.

emily: mid-term we should change scheduler objective: currently it optimizes avg latency vs throughput. we need a tail-aware objective (weighted p95/p99) and a cost for kernel transitions. scheduler should also use sequence-length distribution to set microbatch window, not a single fixed ms.

maria: I'll draft an RFC with replay numbers, profiling artifacts, and three candidate mitigations: (1) dynamic route caps + truncation, (2) kernel pinning for long-seqs, (3) adaptive microbatching by seq-length. aiming to post by EOD.

sophia: small experiment result: reducing microbatch_ms from 32 -> 16 on a canary reduced p99 by ~18% without throughput loss for our test workload. attaching perf graphs in the RFC.

karthik: action items: (A) ops to push canary with truncation + pin (B) emily to prototype tail-aware scheduler objective (C) maria to open RFC w/ numbers. I'll keep monitoring. :eyes:
